ei.title: Chapter 5-15: The Harsh Cure for Inflation
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: Money loses value when inflation takes place; hence, those with large amounts of money encourage a strong government response to inflation. Governments respond by raising interest rates to discourage the creation of additional money through loans. As other loans are paid back, with fewer people taking out new loans, money disappears from circulation, reducing the ability of people to buy things and, thereby, reducing the inflationary pressure. For people and businesses with outstanding loans, the increased cost that results can be disastrous. Increased expenses and bankruptcies lead to job loss, and consequently, more people unable to pay for their homes, cars and other loans. This leads to another round of defaults and subsequent contraction in the money supply. This cure for inflation may bring as much or more hardship than the inflation, but the hardship falls on people with little power to influence policy.

For people and businesses with outstanding loans, the increased cost that results can be (C)[beneficial / disastrous]. Increased expenses and bankruptcies lead to job loss, and consequently, more people unable to pay for their homes, cars and other loans. This leads to another round of defaults and subsequent contraction in the money supply. This cure for inflation may bring as much or more hardship than the inflation, but the hardship falls on people with little power to influence policy.

Governments respond by raising interest rates to ②<u>discourage</u> the creation of additional money through loans. As other loans are paid back, with fewer people taking out new loans, money disappears from ③<u>circulation</u>, reducing the ability of people to buy things and, thereby, reducing the inflationary pressure. For people and businesses with outstanding loans, the increased cost that results can be ④<u>beneficial</u>. Increased expenses and bankruptcies lead to job loss, and consequently, more people unable to pay for their homes, cars and other loans. This leads to another round of defaults and subsequent contraction in the money supply. This cure for inflation may bring as much or more hardship than the inflation, but the hardship falls on people with little power to influence policy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 미상환 대출의 늘어난 비용은 파멸적(disastrous)인데 이로운(beneficial)은 부적절.
det.analysis:
① <u>encourage</u> (부추기다) — 많은 돈을 가진 이들이 강한 대응을 부추긴다, 적절
② <u>discourage</u> (억제하다) — 추가 자금 창출을 억제하려 금리 인상, 적절
③ <u>circulation</u> (유통) — 돈이 유통에서 사라진다, 적절
④ <u>beneficial</u> (이로운) — 원문 disastrous(파멸적인). 늘어난 비용이 파멸적이라는 맥락에서 beneficial 부적절 ←정답

questions.passage: Money ①<u>loses</u> value when inflation takes place; hence, those with large amounts of money encourage a strong government response to inflation. Governments respond by raising interest rates to ②<u>promote</u> the creation of additional money through loans. As other loans are paid back, with fewer people taking out new loans, money disappears from circulation, reducing the ability of people to buy things and, thereby, reducing the inflationary pressure. For people and businesses with ③<u>outstanding</u> loans, the increased cost that results can be disastrous. Increased expenses and bankruptcies lead to job loss, and consequently, more people unable to pay for their homes, cars and other loans. This leads to another round of ④<u>defaults</u> and subsequent contraction in the money supply. This cure for inflation may bring as much or more hardship than the inflation, but the hardship falls on people with little power to influence policy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 금리 인상은 자금 창출을 억제(discourage)하는데 촉진(promote)은 부적절.
det.analysis:
① <u>loses</u> (잃다) — 인플레이션 시 화폐가 가치를 잃는다, 적절
② <u>promote</u> (촉진하다) — 원문 discourage(억제하다). 자금 창출을 억제하려 금리를 올린다는 맥락에서 promote 부적절 ←정답
③ <u>outstanding</u> (미상환의) — 미상환 대출이 있는 개인과 기업, 적절
④ <u>defaults</u> (채무 불이행) — 또 한 차례의 채무 불이행, 적절

questions.passage: Money loses value when inflation ①<u>takes</u> place; hence, those with large amounts of money encourage a strong government response to inflation. Governments respond by raising interest rates to discourage the creation of additional money through loans. As other loans are paid back, with fewer people taking out new loans, money disappears from ②<u>circulation</u>, reducing the ability of people to buy things and, thereby, reducing the inflationary pressure. For people and businesses with ③<u>settled</u> loans, the increased cost that results can be disastrous. Increased expenses and bankruptcies lead to job loss, and consequently, more people unable to pay for their homes, cars and other loans. This leads to another round of defaults and ④<u>subsequent</u> contraction in the money supply. This cure for inflation may bring as much or more hardship than the inflation, but the hardship falls on people with little power to influence policy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 비용이 파멸적인 것은 미상환(outstanding) 대출 때문이지 청산된(settled) 대출이 아니다.
det.analysis:
① <u>takes</u> (발생하다) — 인플레이션이 발생할 때, 적절
② <u>circulation</u> (유통) — 돈이 유통에서 사라진다, 적절
③ <u>settled</u> (청산된) — 원문 outstanding(미상환의). 비용이 파멸적인 것은 미상환 대출 때문이므로 settled 부적절 ←정답
④ <u>subsequent</u> (뒤이은) — 뒤이은 통화 공급 축소, 적절

questions.passage: Money loses value when inflation takes place; hence, those with large amounts of money encourage a strong government response to inflation. Governments respond by raising interest rates to discourage the creation of additional money through loans. As other loans are paid back, with fewer people taking out new loans, money disappears from circulation, reducing the ability of people to buy things and, thereby, __________. For people and businesses with outstanding loans, the increased cost that results can be disastrous. Increased expenses and bankruptcies lead to job loss, and consequently, more people unable to pay for their homes, cars and other loans. This leads to another round of defaults and subsequent contraction in the money supply. This cure for inflation may bring as much or more hardship than the inflation, but the hardship falls on people with little power to influence policy.
